column1: # ⛔ PARSE-COST-RATCHET's message has always ended "… or record it as irreducible with the
# measurement that proves it (`.20` acceptance)" — and until ENGINE-UNIVERSAL-SERVICES.36 there was
# NOWHERE to record it. A rise always failed, with no typed outcome between "eliminate it" and
# "bypass the gate". That asymmetry pressures a correctness fix into being abandoned or a gate into
# being skipped, which is the same shape as SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2k's missing `accepts_invalid`
# manifest class: the instrument could hold one direction of a claim and not the other.
# ⛔⛔ THIS IS NOT A WAIVER FILE. A row does not say "ignore this rise"; it says "this EXACT rise,
# from this EXACT number to this EXACT number, is explained by a NAMED INVARIANT which the gate
# RE-EVALUATES on the fresh measurement". Three properties keep it from becoming a rubber stamp:
#   * from/to are exact integers, so a row cannot cover any rise but the one it was written for;
#   * `invariant` must name one of the predicates coded into scripts/check_parse_cost_ratchet.sh —
#     accepting a rise of a NEW SHAPE therefore takes a code change with its own task leaf, not a
#     new line in a data file;
#   * the invariant is re-checked against the run's own numbers. If it stops holding, the gate
#     fails and says the acceptance's own justification is gone.
# ⚠️ A row is LIVE only while the baseline it names is still the baseline. Once the rise has been
# accepted and `sv_parse_cost_rebaseline` promotes the new measurement, the row matches no rise and
# stops being re-derived — it stays as the AUDIT TRAIL for why the baseline moved upward, which is
# the one thing a promoted baseline can no longer tell you.
# ⛔⛔ AND A ROW CANNOT SILENTLY WIDEN ITS OWN SCOPE (`SV-CORPUS-GRAD.13c.2w`). The fourth
# invariant, `contained_in_introduced_subgraph`, is not an identity over three totals — it asks
# whether every rule whose entries ROSE is reachable, in the measured grammar's own reference
# graph, from the rules the change INTRODUCED. That scope is data, so it lives in the row, in the
# `introduced` column, and the check is two-sided: a scoped invariant with no scope REFUSES, and an
# unscoped invariant carrying one REFUSES too (write `-`). A scope in the gate instead of the row
# would let one code change quietly re-scope every past acceptance.
#   from/to     the exact baseline and measured values this acceptance covers
#   invariant   the coded predicate that explains the rise (see INVARIANTS in the gate script)
#   leaf        the task leaf that owns the measurement
#   why         one line, for a reader
#   introduced  space-separated rule names the change adds a reference to, for a SCOPED invariant;
#               `-` for an invariant that takes no scope
